And I -- that is not what I'm attempting to ask this witness about. I'm only asking him, as Your Honour the Presiding Judge directed me, in relation to whether I provided him with the document and whether he marked it. And that is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the Prosecution to tell me whether the questions it is asking are designed to establish new evidence with respect to what we've already heard and whether this examination will bring us any new elements, because if that is the case then we'll come back to Rule 76(B); that is to say, if any confidential matter was disclosed, I think during the meeting that you had with him does bring up the question of a certain amount of confidentiality. So if this was only used to establish new evidence, then the Prosecutor must present evidence any testimony, document, or any material so provided. So it seems to me that the witness, who also enjoys rights, might consider that his meeting with you was confidential and therefore to reveal the contents of a private conversation he had with you might serve to prejudice the witness. So I should like to draw your attention to that particular point. You can, of course, ask him peripheral questions to confirm that you actually saw him and had a meeting but not go beyond that, especially as I've already said, that the witness could go back to the question, if we should so decide, and the Chamber always has the power to have the witness recalled in due course, at a later date. So the witness has told us that he remembers what happened very well, that his memory does not need to be refreshed. He answered the questions in a very precise manner and even gave us things that were contested but were shown to be interesting with respect to the Defence, that he was no longer a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade in June. So we have a collection of elements which leads us to find that the witness has told us a certain amount of truth. He's answered yes to your questions. So you can go on -- or rather, we should end there, because it seems that we're going to have another witness. The next witness is a mother; she has children, and she has to get back home. So perhaps we could end there and recall the witness in due course to come back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's -- Your Honour referred to Rule 76(B). There's no Rule 70 -- or sorry, the transcript says 76(B). There is no Rule 70(B)-issue here of confidential information or using it to generate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said 70(B), not 76(B), 70(B).

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I can finish this very quickly. I only have two more questions in relation to that and two which Ms. Residovic raised, and it's only -- the Prosecution just wishes to clarify the words "just ignored." That's the limit of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness BA, you told us that we had a conference on Monday and Sunday. Did I provide you with a document on Sunday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Whose statement was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did I give you instructions in relation to that statement, to do something with it overnight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To sign certain parts with which I did not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you make markings on the document, the statement I gave you, on Sunday to bring back to the Prosecution on Monday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just wish to show the document to the witness, have him identify the markings, and have it marked for identification. I don't propose to tender it, only for the purposes of a later application we wish to bring. Just so we don't lose the document and the witness can in fact identify that he mark add particular document; that's it. I'm not trying to tender the evidence inside it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading the English transcript. And he said that he did have knowledge of the document but that that document -- that there were certain elements that he only recognised partially; that is to say, he didn't confirm all of it. So you are -- went on to ask him whether he gave you back the document; he said he did. So that is sufficient. You've no need to go beyond that, because otherwise he's going to say there was one part that I was in agreement with, another part I didn't agree with, and we would enter into a debate again. So let's leave the document. Now, if we recall the witness at a later date, then we can go into matters further. But with respect to the weight of the document, the witness said something -- the contents of the document. I'm sorry -- He said that he read the document but that he didn't recognise the document in its entirety. And that was, I think, on line 56, at 16.23. Now, if there are no further questions, would you like to respond to remarks made by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just wanted it marked for identification so that if the witness is recalled we don't lose the document and there's no dispute between anyone as to what document he actually marked. That's all I want to do; him to identify that he marked it and put it into the Court's custody so the Prosecution doesn't have it any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you have already clearly stated to the Prosecution that he cannot introduce a document in this way. The Prosecution has a completely different position than the Defence. The Prosecution cannot introduce anything into the courtroom without having disclosed it beforehand to the Defence, and the Prosecution has clearly told us that he never disclosed a document marked in that way to the Defence. So I think that you've already resolved the issue, and could you please confirm your ruling and decision. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we have to follow a certain procedure regarding this document. The document that was disclosed in its entirety to the Defence. But, of course, the Defence doesn't have the markings that we're talking about now. So in view of the fact that the witness introduced some changes, modifications, it would be advisable if you -- to let the Defence see the document so that they could gain all the necessary information and then file a motion in writing after their observations and we will decide whether to admit it into evidence or not. As I've already said, we don't exclude the possibility of having this witness recalled in due course. So the document with its notes should be communicated to the Defence because although they have been disclosed, the document -- it was without the markings. So they can read through the document with the markings and might have some observations to make. If, by hypothesis, the document mentioned, for example, a fact that took place when the witness was not present, then this challenges the credibility of the document itself. That is a hypothetical. But as it's already 5.00 p.m., would you like to say anything with respect to the interventions made by the Defence a moment ago? Because you said you did wish to respond to two observations made by them. I'm not quite sure which. But you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not attempting to introduce it into evidence now or at any point. I just want to witness to identify it. There is no -- the witness has not written on it. He's just put yellow marks on it. That's -- I just want him to identify that this is his so that we don't lose it at any other point. Then the Defence can have a look at it. It doesn't matter. That's all. I don't want it into evidence. Just so that we don't lose it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Re, we've -- you've tried to tender this document in the course of the past three days and the Chamber has said no. Now, it's 5.00 p.m. You're trying again to raise the debate again. What I told you was that we will have the Defence look at the document and hear their views on it, and then we will make a ruling. But for the moment the document will not be tendered into evidence. We'll just give it an identification mark. But you've been trying to force the issue, to force the Trial Chamber to accept the document for the past three days. We said at the very outset that within the frameworks of an examination-in-chief you can't produce a previous statement, prior statement, a written prior statement. So we've already broached the matter, and now you're coming back to it. And I indicated that you should provide the Defence with the document for it to be able to make its observations. There might be certain paragraphs which seem to be wrong with respect to the document produced earlier on, and there might be a point of law. So we'll have to look into that. And we'd like to hear the observations of the Defence. So the document is placed at standby. Let the Defence have a chance to look at it. We'll ask for their observations. And then have it admitted or not in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must correct the record. The Prosecution has not been attempting to introduce this document into evidence at any point. This is a copy, a B/C/S copy of the witness's statement in which he made some markings, some highlights. That is all. I only want him to identify that he has marked it. That is as far as I want to go today, so that we don't lose the document. We seem to be at cross-purposes here. The Prosecution is not attempting to tender it, only to have it marked for identification. It doesn't go into evidence. Your Honour, I think, is talking about a different document. That's as far as I want to go. He identifies it -- this is a document I marked. We show it to the Defence. And then if there is a motion later, there's a motion later. And that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have rarely been placed in this kind of position. We don't want to have the document shown to the witness, nor do we wish to have the document marked. You made a ruling, a decision, and we should like to ask the Prosecutor to understand that, to understand that you yourself have ruled on the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we do it right at the very end, after I've finished -- after I've asked my questions in re-examination and I don't have anything else to ask him. Could it possibly be shown to him then for the purposes of he marked it and that's it, so that there's no question of my influencing the witness in any way or refreshing his memory. Could we do it right at the end?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's already answered the question. He said he had a document but the document -- that he recognised certain elements in the document, and he said that he initialled the document. Now, can the witness tell us that he had the document in his hands given to him by the Prosecution, and that he made certain indications on the document? Can he tell us that; yes or no, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something in respect to that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As they said that time was running out and I was a little tired, I don't think I marked in everything. He asked me questions about the portion that I have marked. And I would like to add one more thing: I do not wish to have my identity disclosed, and I was shown this ten minutes before I entered court.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters really apologise, but they're just not able to follow the witness because they can't hear him. There's something wrong with the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's answered the question I was asking of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you have a document given to you by the Prosecution and did you place markings with your own hand on the document? So it's yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We take note that the document that has been placed on standby was marked by the witness. However, the witness said that his principal preoccupation was not to have his identity disclosed; he was worried about that. The Chamber reassured him. We told him that all necessary protective measures had been undertaken so that nobody had access to the contents of the meeting and that he was never referred to by name. He was always referred to by a pseudonym, by initials. So we issued assurances to the witness that confidentiality would be -- would remain intact and his identify would not be revealed. Now, if there are no further direct questions for the witness, we're going to allow the witness to leave the courtroom. I should just like to tell him that he might be recalled one day in due course, at a later date, and that the Chamber will decide that based on various facts and that if he is recalled he'll be asking questions by the Trial Chamber. Has the witness understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution wishes to re-examine the witness. Those last questions were, with leave, on two areas which Mrs. Residovic raised in her cross-examination. It will only take a few minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two questions then, with respect to the cross-examination, what was covered in the cross-examination. Go ahead with your questions. Let's hear the question and we'll see whether it's already been asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness BA, Mrs. Residovic asked you about information you had on several people who had been prosecuted for pretending to be members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. I'm seeking clarification of that, to assist the Trial Chamber in its determination of the truth. What can you tell the Trial Chamber about the courts in which these people were prosecuted, who these people were, and who prosecuted them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, would you answer the question, because it refers to a question posed by the Defence, whether you knew that anybody had been prosecuted. If you know about that, tell us. If not, tell us again; say you don't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who those people were. I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness BA, Mrs. Residovic started her questioning to you by saying that she hadn't met you before and met you only once for ten minutes. I want to ask you whether you have had any contact with either Mr. Ibrisimovic before or any investigators or legal people connected with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, before answering the question, the question deals with your personal life and the issue of confidentiality. So if you think you can answer, go ahead. If you don't think you can, then don't answer. It was just a question to know whether you ever met anybody from the Defence earlier on. You've met them here for a period of ten minutes. But the question is whether you ever met them earlier on. So it's up to you to answer or not to answer, because it has to do with the issue of confidentiality. The Defence has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecutor is insinuating something he insinuated earlier on in the course of the afternoon. And I should first, with the Court's indulgence, like to state -- to give the names of my investigators so that the witness could be able to answer the question, whether he met those individuals before or not, if he wishes to answer. So do you give me permission to do so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you want to communicate that, it's up to you. You're free to do so. I don't want to authorise you to do so or to prevent you from doing so. If you wish to state the names, go ahead; you're free to do so. And then we're going to ask the witness whether the names mean anything to him, whether they ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mustafa Polutak and Vesna Kreso are the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you've heard the names spoken by the Defence. They gave you two names, Mustafa Polutak and Vesna, and they are members of the investigating Defence team. So have you ever met them or not; yes or no, or you have nothing to state?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have not met them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That doesn't fully answer my question. My question was Mr. Ibrisimovic or any legal people, not just investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So the question, Witness BA, was have you met --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour. Microphone for the President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to tell the Prosecution that it is a delicate matter because it has to do with the rights of the Defence. So we're asking attorneys to say what they do, who they meet, and so on, and that seems to me to give rise to problems. But let's hear what the Defence has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness already said yesterday -- or rather, in the course of this afternoon, he said that he met the Defence for less than ten minutes the first time, and I can repeat the names of my investigators: Amila Imamovic and Lejla Sijercic. If those names seem familiar to the witness at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So does the witness know the assistants of the Kubura Defence? Does he recognise the names; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should like now to enter into the record that this is improper behaviour on the part of the Prosecution because he is hurling accusations and conducting an investigation into the conduct and behaviour of the Defence, and I call upon Your Honours to defend the rights of the Defence teams. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mrs. Residovic put into issue in her first question to the witness the fact that she had met the witness for ten minutes only once and at the end said to the witness, "Didn't I tell you -- can't we tell you to tell only the truth during your evidence?" The Defence put this into issue. I'm entitled to ask the witness to clarify whether he has met -- and she -- and her question was directed towards her -- to clarify whether he had at any time met other members of the Defence. That's as far as I wish to take it. And it's go so far -- Mr. Ibrisimovic hasn't said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think we should end the debate there. The witness told us that he had a ten-minute interview with the Defence and the Defence confirmed that they met the witness for ten minutes. Let's leave the matter. There. That completes the examination. Witness, you'll be able to go back home. I don't know when you have your flight home, but the relevant service will see to that. As I've already told you, I think, we might have occasion to see you back here. But anyway, bon voyage back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that you're going to introduce a new witness, Prosecution, aren't you? It's quarter past 5.00. We can go on working until -- or rather, we're going to take a break in about 25 minutes and then resume at 6.00. The Prosecution has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: All right. Your Honours, may I suggest to take the break now and then we can use the remaining time more efficiently. However, there's one -- another issue my colleague wants to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday I attempted -- I foreshadowed tendering three photographs, P16, P17, and P18. I was just trying to do it before the witness left in case there was any difficulty. We have provided copies to the registry. The requisite numbers. May I formally tender those three photographs, P16, P17, and P18 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour. Microphone, for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was saying that we had three exhibits, P16, 17, and 18. They are photographs taken from the air of the area. I don't suppose the Defence has any objections to having these photographs tendered into evidence. May we have the numbers, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P16: Photograph bearing ERN number 01249067; Exhibit P17: Photograph bearing ERN number 01249070; Exhibit P18: Photograph bearing ERN number 01248907.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The exhibit number -- P16 becomes P17; P17 becomes P18; and P18 becomes P19. We're now going to take a break for 25 minutes and shall resume at quarter to 6.00. So back here in court at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. It's ten to 6.00. And we will work until 7.00 p.m., and we will stop at 7.00 p.m. As you know, the interpreters have to finish at 7.00. Tomorrow and the day after we won't be having hearings, since there is a Plenary Session. We will see each other again on Monday at 2.15. We will work until Friday and then we'll have a three-week recess. The Trial Chamber will hand down its decisions very rapidly with regard to the motions submitted. And as far as the pending motions are concerned, I invite the parties to comment on them. We have a new witness; could we have the witness in the courtroom, please. As far as this witness is concerned, how long does the Prosecution think their examination will take?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution anticipates that the examination-in-chief will last about one and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, could you please stand up. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what your first and last name is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Katica Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 10th of October, 1973.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you married or single?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What are you by profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a housewife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A housewife. Very well. Which town do you live in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where? In which town?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which town do you live in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Virovitica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. You're going to read out the solemn declaration now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'd like to inform the witness that she has just taken the solemn declaration and will be asked questions first by the Prosecution and then by the Defence. The witness has the duty to tell the truth. If the witness gives false testimony, she could be prosecuted and proceedings may be initiated for contempt of court. In order to avoid such measure, it would be better to speak the truth. Witness, I think I have -- I think you have some children. You have a family situation which is such that you can't stay over the weekend. You have to return; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you won't be able to return -- you won't be able to come back here on Monday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given the situation, we'll commence with the examination and we have to find another date for the witness to return. She is a housewife. She has to look after her children. There are no objections to be raised by the Defence? Very well. Madam, please sit down. And the Prosecution is going to ask you some questions. The Prosecution has an hour at its disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mrs. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, you have just been asked by Your Honour, the Presiding Judge, when you -- when you were born. Can you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: The 10th of October, 1973.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Chamber where you were born.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: In Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what's your maiden name.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, where did you live in the beginning of April 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: In Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And for how long have you lived in Miletici in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Until the attack against my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In April -- in early April 1993, Mrs. Kovacevic, who were your family members, parents, brothers, and sisters, if any?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I had my parents, my brother, and a sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And were your family members living with you in Miletici?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No. They were living abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In early April 1993, was your brother with you living in Miletici?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber about the name of your brother.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Vlado Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The village of Miletici, Mrs. Kovacevic, in which municipality is it located?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: In the municipality of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber - a rough estimate is efficient, Mrs. Kovacevic - how long villagers were living in Miletici in the beginning of 1993 -- in the beginning of April 1993.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: 20 or 25, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Were these 20 or 25 villagers all of the same ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And what ethnicity were they?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether there have been any further Croat villages in the immediate neighbourhood of Miletici.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Were there any Muslim villages in the immediate neighbourhood of Miletici?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please describe to the Trial Chamber how the relationship between the Croats in Miletici and the Muslims in the immediate neighbourhood in early April 1993 has been.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the relationships were good up until the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: You were talking about the attack. Can you please tell us, Mrs. Kovacevic, what you have done on the 24th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as usual, we were working in the house, working on the land, performing house chores; that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And what have you done, Mrs. Kovacevic, in the evening of the 24th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: We were drinking coffee at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Whilst you were drinking coffee, what did happen?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: We heard that these people had arrived in our village, and someone went to the village. My mother went, and we followed her. And we did not return home after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, you are referring to "these people." Who are "these people"?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to Akif Suljic and Dedo Suljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: What happened after these two people have arrived in Miletici?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, they came to us up there and they said that the Mujahedin had gone to see their girlfriends in the Skomorje village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And what did you do, Mrs. Kovacevic, after you got this information?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we spoke to them there. They said they wouldn't do anything to us. They said we shouldn't be afraid, that we shouldn't be upset. And after a while you could hear the sound of shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Where have you been when you could hear the sound of shooting?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were there in the middle of the village, with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, I'm now going to show you a photograph, and I wish you to identify the photograph and to describe what you can see on the photograph. It will appear on the screen as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Mr. President, I would like to ask my colleague, before he proceeds with his examination, could he tell us who took this photograph and when. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honours, my learned colleagues from the Defence side, the photograph was taken in the course of the investigation against the accused. It was taken in April 2002, and it was taken by Dutch photographers on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, the photograph in front of you, can you please tell the Trial Chamber what you can see on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I can see the place that we were in. I can see the house that we rented. That's where they took us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please first tell the Trial Chamber what village we are seeing on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: This is the village of Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please describe - and I would like you to use the numbers on the photograph - where you went after you got the information on the arrival of Mujahedin and other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were in the middle of the village. I can't see the number here. We went into the house, number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, there are numbers in blue and in red. Can you please clarify for the Trial Chamber which number, either in blue or in red, you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: In red.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: What was the time, Mrs. Kovacevic, when you ran to the house which is marked as number 2 in red on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know at what time we went there. When they attacked our village, we fled to that house, but I don't know at what time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Was it in the morning? Was it in the afternoon? Or was it towards the evening?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: It was after 1800 hours. It was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And who was the owner of the house at the time you were just identifying as the house marked with the red number 2?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: The owner of the house was Stipo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, can you please with a big black texter write on the photograph that the house identified as red number 2 is the house of Stipo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Should I mark it here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: You can mark it at the very bottom of the photograph, where you have the white space.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The house to the left of the house of Stipo Pavlovic, the house with a grey roof, who was the owner of this house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you mean the small house here or the one over here, which is a little further up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: There's one house to the left of the house which is marked with a red number 2. It has a grey roof. Who was the owner of this house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Does it have a number, the one up here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right. Can you, however, tell us who has been the owner of that house at the time?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if it has a number, if it's number 1, then the owner was Bozo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, I'm referring to the house on the left side, on the other side of the house with a red marking number 2.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Sreco Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Is this the house between the red marking number 2 and the red marking number 3?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's Sreco Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please again write this at the very bottom of the photograph and encircle the house, please.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And finally, Mrs. Kovacevic, can you please tell the Trial Chamber who was the owner at the time of the house which is marked with the red number 3.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Ivo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you again, Mrs. Kovacevic, write at the very bottom the name of the owner with the house encircled with the red number 3.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And can you please draw lines between the houses, between the three houses you just have identified, and the names you have written at the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, I'm asking you to draw a line between the name -- the names -- you have written at the very bottom of the photograph and the respective house which you have identified. So if you have, for example, the house number 2 marked with a red number 2, you draw a line between the house with the red number 2 and the name of the owner of that house.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And can you do the very same with the two other houses, please.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The Prosecution wishes to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Usher, would you show the photograph to the Defence counsels and the accused. Show it to the accused as well, please. You wish to intervene?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has no objections, but I think that for us to be able to follow the exhibits better, it would perhaps be a good idea if the witness sign the document and place a date by the signature as well. But if she doesn't do so, we don't have any objection to the exhibit being tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right. Can the photograph please, again, be given to the witness to sign it and to date it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you tell me what the date is today, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Today, Mrs. Kovacevic, is the 10th of December.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, may we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit number is P19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we have the exhibit, which has now been numbered, and it is P19. Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, when you gathered between the houses you just have identified, what was happening?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: When we gathered there, in the middle of the village, what happened was that they attacked. And we fled to take refuge in the house of Stipo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Who was attacking the village of Miletici?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: The Mujahedin attacked and the army, the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The Mujahedin, how can you describe individuals which are -- you are referring to as Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were dark. They had beards. And they couldn't speak our language very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Do you have still a recollection, Mrs. Kovacevic, of how many soldiers attacked Miletici on the 24th of April, 1993? I'm talking about rough numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No. I can't remember that. We fled into the house. We were in shock. And I really don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In which house have you fled?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: We fled to Stipo Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And beside you, who fled in Stipo Pavlovic's house?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: There was also my brother, my parents, my sister, and there were some other local inhabitants. I can't give you their names. I don't know everybody who was there, but all my family were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Was Stipo Pavlovic himself in that house as well?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was in his own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After you found shelter in the house of Stipo Pavlovic, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: What happened was that they said we should open up. We didn't dare open up and we stayed there. They bashed on the windows. We didn't dare open. And Stipo Pavlovic went to the door. He had a rifle and he killed one of them. And then they took us all outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: What happened to Stipo Pavlovic after he had killed one of the Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what happened was that they threw a bomb inside and Stipo Pavlovic was dead on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Who threw a bomb inside?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: My question was: Who threw a bomb inside?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we don't know who threw the bomb. We were in the other room, and we don't know who threw it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether it was one of the attacking soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Yes, it was one of them. But I don't know who, whether it was the Bosnian army or whether it was the Mujahedin. I don't know who actually threw the hand grenade inside, but one of them did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: You just told us a few seconds ago that you -- after Stipo Pavlovic has been killed you went out. Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: They took us out underneath Sreco Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, I am now going to show you a further photograph. The respective photocopies are available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecution tell us, please, who took the photograph and when, because I'm sure the Defence wants to know because they wanted to know for the P19 exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right, Your Honours. This is the very same situation as with the previous photograph; it has been taken in April 2002 by the Dutch photographers on behalf of the Prosecution in the course of the investigation against the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, you were telling us that you were gathering underneath Sreco Pavlovic's house. Can you please first tell the Trial Chamber what you can see on the photograph which is now in front of you.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can see the village. I can see houses. I can see Sreco's house, the one we were taken to below.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right. Which village are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the village of Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Right. You were just telling us that you can see Sreco Pavlovic's house. Can you please encircle the house you can identify as Sreco Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please again write the name of Sreco Pavlovic at the very bottom of this photograph and draw a line between the house and the name.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please now describe and tell the Trial Chamber where you gathered.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: We gathered just below this house, Sreco Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Who was gathering there and how many people?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean when they took us out of the house or before that? I'm not quite sure what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I mean after you have been taken out of the house and after the killing of Stipo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, they took us all out below that house, those of us who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: How many people are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to 20, 25 perhaps. I'm not quite sure how many local inhabitants lived there, how many of us were there. 20; 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Were all Croat villagers gathering at this spot -- on this spot?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, they took us all out and brought us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: After you had gathered on the spot you were just describing, what happened to you then?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, they tied our hands, and we had to stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Have the hands of all Croat villagers which were gathering at the spot you were just detailing been tied up?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They tied all our hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: At this point in time, Mrs. Kovacevic, was your brother -- at this point in time, Mrs. Kovacevic, was your brother Vlado with you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what --

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. What do you want me to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber, Mrs. Kovacevic, what at this point in time happened to your brother Vlado.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was tied too. They called him out and took him off, made him kneel down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, do you need a break at this point in time? The Trial Chamber is certainly very well prepared to have a short break.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No. I can carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened to your brother or what your brother Vlado did prior to him being selected to kneel.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: When they took us out of the house, my brother started to escape. And one of them hit him in his head and brought him in front of us to kneel down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: One of them; who are "them"?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: One of the Muslim army members. I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Talking about yourself, Mrs. Kovacevic, and talking about the other Croat villagers, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: We stayed there. They brought my brother down there. And we had to kneel down, all of us, underneath that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And whilst you were kneeling down, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: They tied us up. We were lying down. They threatened us. They took some pieces of rope as if they were about to hang us. They showed us their long knives and they placed their knives underneath our throats to show us that they would slit our throats.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Again, Mrs. Kovacevic, please feel free to ask whether you wish to have a break.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: No, thank you. I can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In your answer you've just given to me, answering my last question, you were saying "they threatened us. They took some pieces of rope as if they were about to hang us." And "they showed us their long knives," and so on and so on. Who are "they"?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Mujahedin did that and their army did that too. We didn't remember them. Both of them did that. I don't know -- I can't remember all the details now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Ante Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Was Ante Petrovic at this point in time with you?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether he was with us at that time. All I know is that he didn't make it -- they didn't make him kneel down with my brother and the rest of us. He wasn't tied up there with us. They had set him apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Prior to them setting him apart, what happened to Ante Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Ante Petrovic was higher up, up there. I don't know, actually. But he wasn't there with us, and they didn't line him up with the rest of us. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Ante Petrovic prior to the attack, did he have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Ante Petrovic had brought a rifle and he asked whose the rifle was. He said it was his. And as far as I was able to see, he had a sticker on it, a sticker on the rifle, like a chequer-board emblem. And they took him away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: When they took him away, did Ante Petrovic still have his weapon?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I can't say, because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Some minutes ago, Mrs. Kovacevic, you were mentioning that your brother Vlado had to kneel down. Can you please describe to the Trial Chamber how it happened that your brother Vlado had to kneel down.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: He was with us up there, and they called our people out one by one and they had to come out and kneel. And at one point they called out a man's name - Ivo Pavlovic - and my brother was above him and he pointed to my brother, and my brother said, "You mean me? Do you want me to come out?" And he said yes, and told him to leave the line and kneel down.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And again, who have been the people who ordered your brother to kneel down?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who they were, whether it was the Mujahedin who ordered him to do that or the Bosnian army. I really don't know. We were in shock and we waited to see what would happen to us. So I don't know who actually ordered him to step out and kneel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Other than your brother Vlado, were there other people ordered to kneel down?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were others. Tihomir Pavlovic and Franjo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: For clarification, the three people ordered to kneel down were Tihomir Pavlovic, Franjo Pavlovic, and your brother Vlado Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, can you please show us on the photograph of the village of Miletici you still have in front of you the spot the place where these three people have been ordered to kneel down.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And can you please at the very bottom of the photograph write down "place where Franjo Pavlovic, Tihomir Pavlovic, and Vlado Pavlovic have been ordered to kneel down."

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Do I have to mark whose house this is? Do I have to write that down too?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Please feel free to do so. Draw a line again between the spots where they were ordered to kneel down, please. And at the very bottom in the white area of the photograph would you please write down "place where Franjo Pavlovic, Tihomir Pavlovic, and Vlado Pavlovic have been ordered to kneel down."

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And can you please draw again a line between this place --

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I forgot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well. No problem.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. After the selection of Franjo, Tihomir, and Vlado Pavlovic, do you know what happened to them? I mean on the evening of the 24th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: We don't know what happened to them. They lined us up two by two to go to Mehurici and they stayed behind us in this kneeling position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wish to tender the map which has been marked by the witness into evidence. And again, can I please ask the witness to date and sign it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness put her initials there and the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Show the Defence and the accused the document. Very well. The Prosecution has another five minutes. Give it a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit number is P20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it will be P20. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Taking into account that there are only five minutes left for today, I will now show the witness two further photographs and will ask the witness to identify what she can see on these photographs. The respective photocopies are available. Again, this photograph has been taken during the very same period of time in April 2002 in the course of the investigation against the two accused by Dutch photographers on behalf of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic, can you please tell the Trial Chamber what you can see on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I can see Stipo Pavlovic's house and Sreco Pavlovic's house in this photograph. We were a little below these houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please tell which house is Stipo Pavlovic's house.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: This one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please again mark this house with a cross and write at the bottom of the photograph "Stipo Pavlovic's house."

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: Where should I place the cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Wherever you wish; just to identify the house of Stipo Pavlovic. And then please draw a line between the cross -- very well, between the cross and your comment at the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The Prosecution wishes to tender this photograph into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has -- can the witness mark this with her initials and the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you show the photograph to the Defence and to the accused. Could I have a number, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit Number P21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this document is P21. It is five to 7.00. It is time to adjourn. Do you have a last question or have you finished with your questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: With your permission, Your Honours, I today would like to show the witness a further photograph. It will take us two to three minutes. And then once the witness is back I will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mrs. Kovacevic - and again, for the information of the Chamber and for the information of the Defence, this photograph has been taken again in April 2002 in the course of the investigation against the accused by the Dutch photographers on behalf of the Prosecution. Mrs. Kovacevic, can you tell the Trial Chamber what you can see on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: I can see Ivo Pavlovic's house in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can you please, in order to save time, just write the name of Ivo Pavlovic on the house. There's the white house. There's efficient space to write the name on it.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And finally, can you please again date and sign this photograph.

utterances.speaker: KATICA KOVACEVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you show the photograph to the Defence and to the accused. Madam Registrar, could we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... P22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document is document P22. Any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours, Mr. President, it's now two to 7.00. The Prosecution will continue the examination-in-chief once the witness will be back. We suggest that the witness will be called after the winter recess, again to continue the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Madam, it will be necessary for you to return to The Hague at a date that has yet to be set since your family situation is such that you have to return home. You will be informed in good time of the date on which you should return. When you return, we will continue with the examination. The Trial Chamber understands that it is difficult for you to testify here, since it brings back memories of difficult events that you lived through. Everyone is aware of this fact, that you have faced up to this. You will probably return in January and we wish you a good return home. Could the usher please accompany the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution has no more comments to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Not at this point in time. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no objections to raise. But since we have a schedule for witnesses only for the following week, we would be grateful if the Prosecution could provide us with a list for the witnesses it intends to call in January. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no objections to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It would be good if we had a plan for the month of January, which would allow the Defence to prepare itself. So since communication is established between the parties in this manner, we will proceed without any problems and we'll avoid the sort of tension we had a while ago. I would like to thank everyone, and until Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th day of December, 2003, at 2:15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.01 p.m.,
